Etched vs NVIDIA: What you need to know
The AI chip battle is getting interesting.

NVIDIA builds GPUs that can handle almost everything training, inference, different models, and workloads.

Etched is taking the opposite approach.

Its Sohu chip is built specifically for Transformer-based AI inference.
The bet is simple:
NVIDIA: Flexibility
Etched: Specialization

Etched claims its Sohu systems can deliver 500K+ tokens/sec on Llama 70B, dramatically above comparable GPU setups but these numbers are still largely company-reported.

I've been waiting two years for this chip.

Back in June 2024, Etched came out of stealth with a pitch that sounded insane: build the chip specifically for transformer inference, not as a general-purpose GPU. One Etched server potentially replacing 160 NVIDIA H100s.

I chose to pay very close attention. Not because I knew they were right — nobody knew — but because the idea made sense.

GPUs won AI because they were already there: massively parallel, programmable, backed by NVIDIA's software ecosystem. Last week was a big one for non-Nvidia inference silicon. Etched and Cerebras had some very exciting updates. 

Etched shipped its first rack to Jane Street, their first customer, who tested it on live trading workloads, and also led their latest fundraise.

What's been impressive is Etched's innovation here. 

On prefill, they run low-voltage inference to pack more compute into the same power budget. On decode, cluster-scale memory allows an entire rack to function as a single, unified machine. 

Cerebras launched CS-4, which achieves up to 30x faster inference compared to GPUs.

7499190915572625408.author: Founderscrowd
7499190915572625408.text:
Etched doubled to $21 billion in a month. Its chip runs one kind of model and nothing else.

Most AI chips are general, ready for whatever architecture wins next. Etched bet the whole company that the transformer is here to stay, and burned that into silicon.

The reward for being right is enormous. A transformer-only chip is far faster and cheaper than one keeping its options open.

The risk is the same size. If the field moves past the transformer, a general chip adapts. This one is scrap.

Jane Street led the round and is also the customer, running the racks.

You trade flexibility for performance and pray the ground does not move.
